llm.summary: The skill's goal (multi‑agent orchestration) matches the files and scripts provided, but the runtime instructions and bundled scripts grant broad, high‑privilege changes to the user's OpenClaw environment (writing configs, creating symlinks, installing a background watcher, modifying openclaw.json to allow subagents, and restarting the Gateway) while not declaring required credentials — review before running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi‑agent orchestration) aligns with the included assets: agent templates, project.json, many AGENTS.md/SOUL.md/IDENTITY.md files and orchestration scripts. Creating workspaces, agent configs, and a watcher is coherent for this purpose. However, the skill performs high‑impact actions (writing ~/.openclaw/*, symlinks, adding agents to openclaw.json and setting main.subagents.allowAgents:["*"], restarting the Gateway) that materially change the host agent environment; those are powerful operations that should be explicitly documented and consented to.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to run setup.sh immediately ("must first execute") and describes automated creation/copying of directories, templates, per‑agent agentDir copies, creation of ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, modification of openclaw.json, and a Gateway restart. These instructions go beyond passive guidance and give the agent permission to modify persistent configuration and system behavior; they also install and recommend a background watcher. The instructions therefore grant broad write/privilege scope over the agent runtime and system scheduler (launchd/systemd/cron) which is high‑impact and outside simple answer/analysis behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in registry metadata (instruction‑only), but the package includes many shell and Python scripts (scripts/setup.sh, watch-install.sh, watch.sh, backups.sh, etc.) that are intended to be executed. Bundling scripts inside the skill and instructing an agent to run them effectively functions as an installer; since the code is local (no remote download URLs shown in the truncated listing) this is lower risk than fetching arbitrary remote archives, but running these scripts will write/modify files and restart services — review the scripts before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required environment variables or primary credential, but the docs/scripts reference model providers and token behavior (openai provider, OPENAI_API_KEY mentioned in troubleshooting) and Telegram notification configuration. The skill will interact with model providers and optionally Telegram if configured, yet it does not declare those credentials as required — this is an inconsistency. Also, writing openclaw.json to set main.subagents.allowAgents:["*"] expands agent permissions and could be disproportionate unless explicitly needed and reviewed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent configuration (symlink ~/.openclaw/skills/team-dispatch → <SKILL_DIR>), creates ~/.openclaw/workspace/tasks/, copies agent templates to ~/.openclaw/agents/<id>, creates ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, modifies agents.list in openclaw.json, and restarts the Gateway. It also installs/instantiates a background watcher (openclaw-cron / launchd / systemd / cron). While always:false (not force‑enabled globally), these changes grant long‑lived privileges and modify the agent environment and scheduling; that persistent footprint is significant and should be consented to and audited.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill contains many scripts and explicit install instructions that will modify your OpenClaw environment: create symlinks, copy agent workspaces into ~/.openclaw/agents/, write ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, change openclaw.json (including main.subagents.allowAgents:["*"]) and restart the Gateway, and may install a background watcher. Those are high‑impact operations. Before running setup.sh or allowing the agent to auto‑execute: 1) inspect scripts/setup.sh, watch-install.sh and watch.sh for exact file writes, restart commands, and any network calls; 2) back up your existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and configs; 3) verify you trust the skill author/source (source is unknown here); 4) if you want to test, run the setup in an isolated environment (VM/container) or perform a dry run by reading the scripts instead of executing them; 5) check for references to provider credentials (OPENAI_API_KEY, Telegram chatId) and decide how/where to supply them — do not provide secrets unless you trust the code and understand what will be transmitted; and 6) consider whether you want openclaw.json modified to allow subagents:["*"] because that broadens which agents can run as subagents. If anything looks unexpected, ask the author for provenance, a minimal install mode, or an explicit list of changes the installer will perform.
